.\CLAUDE.md:163:    3. **PARTIAL-OVERLAP** — incumbent and candidate cover overlapping function via DIFFERENT MECHANISMS. Disposition: **CASE-BY-CASE**, typically CITE-PATTERN-ONLY or STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-C mem0 (fact-extraction-based memory) vs eee graphiti (temporal-KG-based) vs mcp-memory (sqlite-vec-based) — same memory layer, different mechanisms. .\CLAUDE.md:165:    4. **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT** — parallel API surfaces but different scopes; both can coexist. Disposition: **INSTALL as ALTERNATIVE (not PRIMARY)** — primary incumbent retains canonical position. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-A openai-agents-python (vs Anthropic `claude-agent-sdk-python` @ HEAD `b512f256`) — Anthropic SDK = direct CC control plane (PRIMARY); OpenAI SDK = provider-agnostic orchestration (ALTERNATIVE). .\CLAUDE.md:167:    5. **ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT** — core primitive GENUINELY-NEW at the surface level but imports parallel ecosystem at the dependency level. .\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:10:    ### CR-12 disposition lattice (5 classes — Wave 134 Fire 27 series codification)
.\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:12:    Beyond the **install-source priority order** (PRIMARY/SECONDARY/TERTIARY) above, every upstream-vs-incumbent relationship falls into ONE of 5 classes. Wave 134 Fire 27 series empirically mapped all 5:
.\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:14:    1. **GENUINELY-NEW** — no Anthropic/incumbent parallel exists for the primitive's scope. Disposition: **INSTALL via CR-12 PRIMARY path** (official-native-channel per CR-6). No further audit needed beyond Probe DAG.
.\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:18:    3. **PARTIAL-OVERLAP** — incumbent and candidate cover overlapping function via DIFFERENT MECHANISMS. Disposition: **CASE-BY-CASE**, typically CITE-PATTERN-ONLY or STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-C mem0 (fact-extraction-based memory) vs eee graphiti (temporal-KG-based) vs mcp-memory (sqlite-vec-based) — same memory layer, different mechanisms. Codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27c_mem0_OUT.txt` STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT conf=0.87.
.\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:20:    4. **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT** — parallel API surfaces but different scopes; both can coexist. Disposition: **INSTALL as ALTERNATIVE (not PRIMARY)** — primary incumbent retains canonical position. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-A openai-agents-python (vs Anthropic `claude-agent-sdk-python` @ HEAD `b512f256`) — Anthropic SDK = direct CC control plane (PRIMARY); OpenAI SDK = provider-agnostic orchestration (ALTERNATIVE). Codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27a_openai_agents_python_OUT.txt` STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT conf=0.89.
.\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:22:    5. **ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT** — core primitive GENUINELY-NEW at the surface level but imports parallel ecosystem at the dependency level. Disposition: **EVALUATE ecosystem cost vs core primitive value** (often CITE-PATTERN-ONLY when ecosystem footprint disproportionate). Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-B langgraph (Pregel BSP graph execution is novel BUT requires `langchain-core>=1.4.0a2` + 6+ langgraph-* sub-package import + LangSmith proprietary recommended). Pattern B HNF disposition at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27b_langgraph_OUT.txt`.
.\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:24:    **Cite class for this 5-class lattice itself**: `constituents=[TIER-3-LOCAL-OPERATOR-DERIVED @ Wave 134 Fire 27-A + 27-B + 27-C codex T1 verdicts, TIER-2 @ existing cardinal-rule-12 scaffolding, TIER-2 @ `citation-discipline.md` rule #8 source-class reduction lattice precedent, TIER-1-DIRECT @ Anthropic + OpenAI + LangChain TIER-1 maintainer evidence]; effective_tier=TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION` per `citation-discipline.md` rule #8 MIN_PRECEDENCE.
.\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:29:    - **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT** vs **DUPLICATE-FUNCTIONALITY**: distinguished by whether both incumbents cover DIFFERENT scopes (PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT — both useful) or SAME scope (DUPLICATE — pick one)
.\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:30:    - **PARTIAL-OVERLAP** vs **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT**: distinguished by whether the DIFFERENT MECHANISMS suggest parallel co-existence (PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT) or competing-implementations (PARTIAL-OVERLAP requires case-by-case)
.\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:31:    - **ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT** is the OPERATIONAL escape valve when a candidate's core primitive is novel but ecosystem footprint creates duplicate-frameworks concern
.\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:34:    - `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/codex-t1-fix-forward-pattern.md` — verdict-disposition lattice (APPROVE/NEEDS-REVISION/REJECT/STUDY-PILOT-NARROW/STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT/CITE-PATTERN-ONLY/REJECT-FOR-FIT/Pattern B HNF) maps to CR-12 lattice as follows:
.\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:35:      - GENUINELY-NEW → APPROVE / STUDY-PILOT-NARROW
.\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:37:      - PARTIAL-OVERLAP → CITE-PATTERN-ONLY / STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT (typical)
.\docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:38:      - PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT → STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT (typical) OR STUDY-PILOT-NARROW

**Hard precondition (before applying .a or .b)**: earlier Axis-4 blockers WIN. If the candidate duplicates an existing shipped primitive (Probe 4 plugin-namespace), collides with plugin namespace, requires an unmet harness/mode assumption (Probe 5 mode-harness-shape), fails Probe 6 (license/registry/build-deps blocker), is SUPERSEDED-BY-X (existing primitive owns the workflow), or is a META-HARNESS competing-framework shape per `docs/verified-avoid.md` Cohort 1, classify under that blocker instead. Probe 7.b is ONLY available for structurally sound primitives that create a genuinely new, non-duplicative workflow.

#### Probe 7.a — DEMAND-ABSENCE (REJECT-FOR-FIT)

What sss workflow / invocation surface / consumer would route through this primitive TODAY? Verify the 3-clause check:
- Cite a specific path (existing or queued)
- Is the candidate's value proposition met by an EXISTING shipped primitive? (e.g., "graphiti MCP already provides FalkorDB temporal KG access" → dbhub adds no marginal value AS A REPLACEMENT)
- Is the candidate displacing or extending? Displacement requires migration plan; extension requires marginal-value evidence

If NO current/queued workflow AND .b 5-clause check (below) does not survive, REJECT-FOR-FIT.a (demand-absence) — REJECT-decisive.

#### Probe 7.b — DEMAND-CREATES-NEW-WORKFLOW (STUDY-PILOT eligible)

A structurally sound primitive may create a genuinely new workflow that no existing sss primitive serves. STUDY-PILOT eligibility requires ALL 5 clauses to hold (codex T1 NEEDS-REVISION conf=0.84 Q2 prescription at `.claude/state/codex_consult_ship27_3_probe7_demand_creates_OUT.txt`):

1. **Named operational use case**: cite the query/workflow and the consumer that would exercise it
2. **Cited local input/source path**: identify the concrete data, repo path, tool surface, or state file (e.g., `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/state/mcp_overhead_audit.jsonl`)
3. **Wiring path**: name the adapter/ETL/config needed to make the primitive consume the source; if wiring is non-trivial, it is part of the pilot cost
4. **Incumbent comparison**: explain why existing shipped primitives or simpler local commands (`rg`, `jq`, GitNexus, Langfuse MCP, graphiti, mcp-memory, one-off Python scripts) do not already satisfy the use case OR are materially worse
5. **Reversible time-box**: define owner, max pilot cost, 30-day success criterion, and retirement path

**Pilot failure**: retire to `disabledMcpjsonServers` if applicable and document in `docs/verified-avoid.md` under the matching failure cohort; create a dedicated retired-pilot / demand-not-realized cohort only after n>=2 same-shape recurrences. NOTE: `verified-avoid.md` Cohort 2 is specifically Probe 6 direct-file/registry blockers per `docs/verified-avoid.md:47-49`; failed demand-pilots do NOT belong there by default. Use the matching failure cohort for retirement (e.g., a pilot that failed because it duplicated an existing primitive retires to Cohort 1 META-HARNESS competing-frameworks).

[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/openai-agents?label=pypi%20package)](https://pypi.org/project/openai-agents/)\\n\\nThe OpenAI Agents SDK is a lightweight yet powerful framework for building It is provider-agnostic, supporting the OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions APIs, as well as 100+ other LLMs.\\n\\n<img src=\\\"https://cdn.openai.com/API/docs/images/orchestration.png\\\" alt=\\\"Image of the Agents Tracing UI\\\" style=\\\"max-height: 803px;\\\">\\n\\n> [!NOTE]\\n> Looking for the JavaScript/TypeScript version? [**Agents**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/agents): LLMs configured with instructions, tools, guardrails, and handoffs\\n1. [**Sandbox Agents**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sandbox_agents): Agents preconfigured to work with a container to perform work over long time horizons.\\n1. **[Agents as tools](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/tools/#agents-as-tools) / [Handoffs](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/handoffs/)**: Delegating to other agents for specific tasks\\n1. [**Tools**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/tools/): Various Tools let agents take actions (functions, MCP, hosted tools)\\n1. [**Guardrails**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/guardrails/): Configurable safety checks for input and output validation\\n1. [**Human in the loop**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/human_in_the_loop/): Built-in mechanisms for involving humans across agent runs\\n1. [**Sessions**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/sessions/): Automatic conversation history management across agent runs\\n1. [**Tracing**](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/tracing/): Built-in tracking of agent runs, allowing you to view, debug and optimize your work"}
